If discovery misses your engine, choose its installation folder. You do not need to pick an executable or configuration file.

Advanced: configure the launch method manually
Register an executable or entry point

Choose how to launch the engine, read its help, then configure model, connection and compatibility checks. After Register succeeds, AioLM saves the connection details automatically. You do not need to create an .engine.json file.

Have a connection setup file?

Import an AioLM setup prepared by the engine or adapter provider. Choosing an executable does not generate this file.

Import AioLM connection setup (.json)

Unpack the adapter folder and select its connection setup JSON (for example *.setup.json). Ordinary engine configuration JSON and model files are not setup recipes. Without a setup file, register manually below.

Local inference server

Connect the selected installed server and model. The app reads the executable's real help, and the model check sends actual JSON and streaming requests to the running local service. This temporary guide example is not a bundled engine.

Register manually without a setup file

Choose the server executable (for example llama-server.exe or llama-server). For a Python engine, choose the python.exe or bin/python used to install it, then add the script path or -m and module name as separate arguments below. Do not select a model (.gguf or .safetensors), installer or ordinary configuration JSON as the executable.

The engine must provide OpenAI-compatible HTTP/SSE, or a separate bridge must provide it. A model compatibility probe is also required. An executable alone is insufficient. Ask the provider for model/port options and an AioLM-compatible probe.
